A1.justification: Both complete 40-page PDFs describe OneForecast and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–G. Text and visual comparison support reliable assessment of the equations, tables, figures, and appendix results.

before.justification: v2 reports original global and regional forecasting experiments, ensemble forecasts, cyclone evaluations, and ablations in Section 3 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains the original forecasting experiments and analyses, including OneForecast results in Tables 1–3 and the additional evaluations in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithm 1, and Appendix E retain the same region-refined graph, multi-stream messaging, neural nested grid, training objective, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WeatherBench2/ERA5 data for global and regional forecasting and the same cyclone cases. The place-name substitution in Appendix F.3 does not change the selected events or their dates.

E2.justification: Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and FuXi remain the Table 1 comparators, and Graph-EFM remains in the regional comparison in Figure 6. Comparator membership also matches throughout the appendix evaluations.

E3.justification: The data splits, resolutions, variables, forecast intervals, evaluation metrics, training budgets, and evaluation sample counts are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C–G.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Table 3, spectral analyses in Figures 7–8, long-horizon analysis, and cyclone case studies. No analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: The 50-member ensemble specification, averaging procedure, and existing statistical reporting are unchanged. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing disclosures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and graphical results match, including OneForecast's 6-hour RMSE of 0.0549 in Table 1 and track-position error of 157 km in Table 7. The appendix forecast maps are also identical.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1, its assumptions and proof in Appendix A, and the mathematical definitions and derivations elsewhere are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified global-regional forecasting, adaptive information propagation, extreme-event prediction, and long-term forecasting.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning high-frequency information, over-smoothing, and boundary forcing are unchanged. Qualifications about lower-resolution cyclone forecasts and limited finetuning also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, training instructions, and code/data access information match. The updated arXiv self-link does not change access to experimental resources.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including Appendix B and the introduction's comparison with Graph-EFM.

P1.justification: Appendix F.3 replaces 'Ito To, Japan' with 'Iwo Jima, Japan' in the description of Yagi's formation. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The place-name edit produces small line-wrapping changes across pages 17–18, and the margin stamp updates. Figures 1–30, Tables 1–7, their captions, and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision consists of a place-name substitution in Appendix F.3 and an updated arXiv stamp, with incidental text reflow. The methods, experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain identical, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
